themes.summary: Safety and security work is turning into standing practice: OpenAI built Control Room so a monitor can halt any agentic research job in about 35 seconds and has given Apollo, METR, Transluce and Goodfire deep internal access to assess its models, while Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve to prove a reply came from committed weights. The threat side is speeding up: the FBI says attackers used the ARTEX agent framework to reach privileged access in under three hours, Google found exploit_agent, a pipeline that turns web-app patches into working exploits with no human in the loop, and Cursor traced its breach to credentials left in agent traces. Defenders are adjusting their clocks in response, as Anthropic cuts its disclosure window from 90 to 30 days because models now rediscover bugs quickly. Kill switches, outside audits, provenance and faster patching are becoming day-to-day lab and network infrastructure.
themes.title: Safety, security and provenance go operational

themes.summary: Always-on personal agents keep picking up real-world reach: Meta's Muse sends email from its own address, Claude reads bank and card data through Plaid, and Grok Bot works with Apple's Mac apps and can now book flights, hotels and rental cars end to end. Money and scale are the newest pieces, with OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet giving agents tokenized cards and Google making Gemini Tasks free for hundreds of millions of users, including Google Pay purchases. The agent is becoming a standing intermediary with its own identity, access and spending, so permissions and site-side controls matter as much as the model.
themes.title: Personal agents get their own computers, accounts and money

The cheap end is crowding too, and Vercel's AI Gateway shows small decision models already handle 26% of requests. Competition is shifting toward price per task and the workloads agents actually run, with mid tiers built to orchestrate cheaper subagents.
themes.title: Closed labs ship new flagships and faster tiers

themes.summary: Agents are moving from single chats to long jobs: parallel agents in ChatGPT Pro, Gemini agents playing Minecraft for 27 hours, durable pi agents and dedicated memory models, and GitHub rebuilding Copilot around parallel agent sessions, now carried by an open Agent Host Protocol so a session continues across devices. The harness is going multiplayer as well: Cursor rebuilt Projects so teammates and their agents share one workspace, and Mistral Studio runs long-lived managed agents with approvals and tracing. Anthropic's write-up of agent memory treats offline "dreaming" as the pass that corrects bad notes and preloads the next session. The hard problems remain state, memory, orchestration and coordination around the model.
themes.title: Agents become long-running, parallel and stateful

The local stack is maturing alongside: llama.cpp and ggml reached 1.0 with a stable API and ABI, and Hugging Face showed a 180B MoE running in 32GB of RAM by streaming experts from SSD. Open release is a normal path to frontier capability, and running it on your own hardware keeps getting more practical.

The work is reaching engineering too: OpenAI models rewrote RTL for AMD's flagship GPU for up to 14% PPA gains, some already sent to manufacturing. Research results are becoming both a capability signal and a product line.

Muse Spaces turns a description into a persistent mini-app, and the flow also runs the other way, as OpenAI lets businesses deploy agents inside ChatGPT and Stripe exposes payments data to agents over MCP. Distribution through existing tools matters as much as raw model quality.
themes.title: Assistants move into the tools people already use

themes.summary: As agents run code and touch production, containment is getting real engineering. Vercel's sandbox challenge surfaced a kernel zero-day, Google offers a microVM per agent, Figma built Nimbus to run tens of thousands of isolated sandboxes, and OpenAI documented how Codex's defaults (workspace writes, broad reads, no network) are enforced on macOS, Linux and Windows and which attacks they still allow. Testing the walls is maturing too, as Perplexity had 12 models try to escape its agent VM. Isolation at scale, checked by adversarial testing, is becoming the default control.
themes.title: Sandboxes and limits for agents that act

themes.summary: Companies are reporting agents that own entire workflows in production, with measured results. SpaceXSI runs five Grok Bots that each own an accounting job behind approval gates, Meta's agents now do 60% of porting ranking-model improvements across its ads fleet with a median 4x cut in training compute, and CVS and Cigna run OpenAI computer-use agents on healthcare admin at cents per task. Microsoft's Autopilot brings the same pattern to the enterprise suite, giving each always-on agent its own identity, manager and audit log. The question is moving from whether agents can do the work to how they are onboarded, supervised and audited.
themes.title: Agents take over whole business processes

items.title: Ramp: making LLM judges agree when grading coding agents

themes.summary: Engineering teams are publishing how they test systems whose output is open-ended. Netflix runs LLM judges in production and aligns them with human ratings over time, Vercel lays out an agent test pyramid with seeded task environments and per-constraint verifiers, and Ramp replaced tests with deliberating LLM judges for its internal coding benchmark, lifting judge agreement from 54% to 94%. Reliable evaluation is becoming its own engineering discipline, and a prerequisite for shipping agents with confidence.
themes.title: Teams build evals and judges for agents

themes.summary: Anthropic has opened its IPO roadshow, with a prospectus showing $17.0B of revenue in Q3 2026, more than 12x a year earlier, and over 11,900 customers paying $100K+ a year. It got there after filing an S-1 to list on Nasdaq as ANT, committing 5% of its shares to a Public Benefit Fund, and handing its Agent Skills standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. A frontier lab going public puts its finances and governance in the open and sets a template for how safety-focused labs raise capital.
themes.title: Anthropic reshapes its governance on the way to an IPO

themes.summary: Agents now write code faster than Git hosting and review were built for. GitHub moved repositories to Azure under agent-driven load and has published the redesign of its Git object storage; OpenAI built Pando, a Rust Git backend for thousands of concurrent pushes from engineers and Codex agents, cutting median push latency by about 80% on a petabyte-scale monorepo. Anthropic built its own source control after merges grew more than tenfold, and teams are answering review load with automation such as Meta's just-in-time tests. Tooling built for human pace is giving way first.
themes.title: Infrastructure strains under agent-scale code
